I’ll outline it so you only touch the phone case and leave the others alone. The exact wording on your screen may differ a bit, but the flow is usually like this:

1) Open the order
- Sign in to your account.
- Go to: “Orders” or “Your Orders.”
- Find order: ODR-113456 (total around $67.98, placed today).
- Click into that order (usually “View details” or clicking the order itself).

2) Start an item-level cancellation
Look for one of these near the top or by the item list:
- “Cancel items”
- “Modify order”
- “Edit items” / “Change items”

Click that. You should now see a list of the items in this order, each with a checkbox or quantity field.

3) Select ONLY the phone case
In the item list, identify:
- “Phone Case – Clear” (SKU-778 / price about $19.99).

Then:
- If there are checkboxes: check the box ONLY for the Phone Case – Clear.
- If there’s a quantity dropdown: set the cancel quantity to 1 only for the phone case.

Double-check:
- The Screen Protector – 3 Pack and Wireless Charger should be:
  - Unchecked, or
  - Having their cancel quantity set to 0 / blank.

4) Choose a reason (if asked)
Many sites show a “Reason for cancellation” dropdown next to each selected item or at the bottom. For the phone case item, select something like:
- “Changed my mind”
- “Ordered by mistake”
- Or similar.

5) Confirm the cancellation
Scroll to the bottom and click:
- “Cancel selected items”
- or “Confirm cancellation,” etc.

Before you click:
- Re-read the confirmation text. It should clearly mention only the phone case (and not all three items).
Then confirm.

6) Verify it worked
After confirming, you should see either:
- A success message like “1 item canceled from your order,” and/or
- An updated order view where:
  - Phone Case – Clear is marked “Canceled” or no longer listed as an active item.
  - Screen Protector – 3 Pack and Wireless Charger still show as “Processing” / “Pending.”

If you want to be extra sure:
- You’ll usually get an email. The subject line often says “Item(s) canceled from your order” and lists only the phone case.

If you tell me what you see on the screen (especially the wording of the cancel page and confirmation), I can sanity-check it before you click the final “Cancel” button, so you don’t accidentally touch the other items.</action>
